title: Gravitational Redshift
description: Light climbing out of a gravity well loses energy, so its frequency falls: clocks below run slow seen from above. In 1959 Pound and Rebka measured it up a 22.5-metre tower. Unlocks the Pound-Rebka Tower and the Cobalt-57 Source.

puzzle.goal: Light climbs a height H in a gravity g. Moving up it loses energy as a ball thrown upward would, in proportion to its own energy divided by c². Write the fraction s of its frequency it loses.
puzzle.name: Gravitational shift over a height
puzzle.ask: Find s in units of 10⁻¹⁵ for Pound and Rebka's tower: g = @{g} m/s², H = @{H} m, c = 2.998e8 m/s.
puzzle.method: A photon of energy E has an effective mass E/c²; climbing H costs it (E/c²)·g·H of energy.
